body:
### Summary

On Windows with a CUDA 12.x driver (`>=528.33, <580`), `--torch-backend=auto` selects `cu129` first and resolves `torch 2.9.0+cu129` with `torchvision 0.2.0` (from 2018) without any warning.

Linux with CUDA 12.x and Windows with a CUDA 13 driver (`>=580`) are unaffected.

### Reproduce

On Windows:

```bash
UV_CUDA_DRIVER_VERSION=560.94 uv pip install torch torchvision --torch-backend=auto
```

On any OS (`requirements.in` contains `torch` and `torchvision`):

```bash
UV_CUDA_DRIVER_VERSION=560.94 uv pip compile requirements.in --torch-backend=auto --python-platform x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
```

- Plain command with no version pins.
- Reproduced with uv 0.13.6 (Python 3.10–3.13) and 0.12.16.
- Reproduced above by simulating the driver via `UV_CUDA_DRIVER_VERSION`, and also observed on a real Windows GPU machine (RTX 3060 Ti).

| Platform & Driver | Selected Index | Resolved torch | Resolved torchvision |
|---|---|---|---|
| Windows, CUDA 12.x (`>=528.33, <580`) | `cu129` | `2.9.0+cu129` | `0.2.0` |
| Windows, CUDA 13 (`>=580`) | `cu132` | `2.14.1+cu132` | `0.29.1+cu132` |
| Linux, CUDA 12.x | `cu129` | `2.13.0+cu129` | `0.28.0+cu129` |

### Impact

- `uv pip install` and `import torchvision` succeed, and basic transforms still work.
- Fails later at runtime with `ImportError` on modern symbols (`InterpolationMode`, `efficientnet_b0`) and missing `torchvision.ops`.
- `torch` itself is also outdated: Windows `cu129` stops at 2.9.0, whereas `cu128` has 2.11.0 and `cu126` has 2.14.1.

### Cause

- `WINDOWS_CUDA_VERSIONS` in `crates/uv-torch/src/backend.rs` tries `cu129` before `cu128` and `cu126` (added in #15416).
- On Windows, the `cu129` index stopped receiving updates at torch 2.9.0 and torchvision 0.23.0 (no 0.24.0 build for torch 2.9.0). On Linux, `cu129` still has matching pairs.
- All PyTorch indexes still host pure-Python torchvision 0.1.6 and 0.2.0 wheels with no torch version constraint.
- Because uv resolves from the first index containing the package, 0.2.0 is the newest torchvision version on `cu129` compatible with torch 2.9.0 (pip on the same index picks 0.1.6).

| Windows Index | Latest torch | Latest torchvision | Resolved Pair (torch + torchvision) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cu126` | `2.14.1+cu126` | `0.29.1+cu126` | `2.14.1+cu126` + `0.29.1+cu126` |
| `cu128` | `2.11.0+cu128` | `0.26.0+cu128` | `2.11.0+cu128` + `0.26.0+cu128` |
| `cu129` | `2.9.0+cu129` | `0.23.0+cu129` (for torch 2.8) | `2.9.0+cu129` + `0.2.0` |

### Workarounds

- `--torch-backend=cu128` → torch `2.11.0+cu128` + torchvision `0.26.0+cu128`
- `--index-strategy unsafe-best-match` → torch `2.14.1+cu126` + torchvision `0.29.1+cu126`
- `torchvision>=0.3` → torch `2.8.0+cu129` + torchvision `0.23.0+cu129`

Related: #12357, #14742, #16386

### Possible fixes

- Lower the priority of (or drop) `cu129` in `WINDOWS_CUDA_VERSIONS`.
- Fall through to the next candidate index if the selected index has no compatible torchvision wheel for the resolved torch version.
- Enforce a minimum version bound for torch-family packages so legacy unpinned wheels (0.1.6 / 0.2.0) are not selected for modern torch.
title: --torch-backend=auto on Windows with CUDA 12.x driver resolves torchvision 0.2.0 (2018)
